INFORMATION.
IN MOTION.

My research explores how information changes as it moves through people, platforms and machines, and how its fidelity to a source might be preserved and measured.

My investigative and creative practice brings a sustained interest in sources, interpretation and how an account takes shape. These four papers develop that inquiry across AI training data, information governance, optical computation and measurement.

Featured publication / July 2026

Information
Fidelity

Can fidelity to a declared source become a reproducible optical measurement with a traceable reference and stated uncertainty?

The monograph proposes separate measures for artefact integrity and content fidelity to a declared source. Experimental validation remains ahead.

How the work connects

Questions carried forward

The July monograph brings three earlier lines of inquiry into a proposed measurement framework. These relationships are part of its theoretical synthesis; the experimental programme is still to be carried out.

Three connected investigations

October 2025 / March 2026

01 / Hypothesis / Research preprint

Training Data Velocity Bias ↗

Could virality skew web training data toward less reliable claims and contribute to language model hallucinations?

The paper proposes that rapidly amplified claims may become overrepresented in web training data. A corpus study and controlled model experiments would test whether this selection contributes to hallucination. The causal link remains a hypothesis.

02 / Proposed framework / Research preprint

Vital Network Science ↗

Could moderating unusually rapid amplification improve information ecosystems while preserving access and user agency?

A proposed feedback governor would moderate rapid amplification using temporary delays, context and changes to recommendations. Seven dimensions of ecosystem health guide the framework, with user override, appeals and public oversight. Its benefits await empirical validation.

27 October 2025 · 25 pages

03 / Conceptual architecture / Research preprint

Photonic Substrate Intelligence ↗

Can optical computation and rewritable physical media support practical neural-network inference and training at scale?

A speculative architecture brings optical computation, separate context and weight media, and holographic training signals into one design. The first tests concern activation power and wavelength-channel isolation. An integrated prototype has yet to be demonstrated.
